headline: Why did Druski play Elizabeth Holmes in a wild SNL parody?
standfirst: Internet comedian Druski made history as the first digital creator to host Saturday Night Live, treating viewers to an unforgettable Elizabeth Holmes spoof.
keyPoints: Druski made history as the first digital content creator to host Saturday Night Live.
He starred in a parody sketch titled 'Dru Can See Everything' focusing on Elizabeth Holmes.
The sketch playfully reimagined the documentary-style interactions featuring Jane Wickline as Holmes.
Druski famously donned whiteface in the sketch to fully embody the Theranos founder.

sections.heading: How did Druski make history on Saturday Night Live?
paragraphs: The late-night comedy landscape shifted when popular digital content creator and comedian Druski took the stage to host Saturday Night Live. Breaking new ground for the iconic NBC show, he became the very first internet personality without a traditional television or movie project to helm the episode as host. Kicking off the night with a memorable cold open and a lively monologue featuring special guest stars, Druski quickly proved that his internet-born comedic timing could seamlessly transition to live network television.

From satirical news panels to clever commercial parodies, the episode showcased a wide variety of original sketches. Druski brought his signature chaotic energy to roles ranging from an overwhelmed birthday guest to a hyper-committed wedding photographer. However, it was a specific pop-culture parody later in the evening that completely stole the show and set social media abuzz with clips and commentary.

sections.heading: What inspired the 'Dru Can See Everything' sketch?
paragraphs: The centerpiece of the night was a brilliant spoof titled 'Dru Can See Everything,' which targeted the much-discussed meta-documentary centering around disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes. The sketch hilariously imagined a fictional timeline where Holmes and her partner, Billy Evans, approached Druski to film their documentary before ultimately working with Nathan Fielder. Cast member Jane Wickline portrayed Holmes with her signature deep-voiced intensity alongside Ben Marshall as Evans.

As the fictional meeting unfolded, Druski immediately called out the couple's unusual demeanor, remarking on their strange and unsettling vibe. True to his comedic style, the host did not hold back his skepticism, telling the camera exactly what he thought of the bizarre dynamic playing out right in front of him.

sections.heading: Why did Druski use whiteface to play Elizabeth Holmes?
paragraphs: In a move that fans had half-predicted during his opening monologue, Druski decided to take on the role of Holmes himself rather than casting someone else. Donning whiteface makeup to channel the tech founder's distinct look, he engaged in a hilariously tense, up-close stare-down reenactment opposite Wickline's Holmes. The back-and-forth dialogue pushed absurd boundaries as the two versions of Holmes debated who was truly being authentic.

The physical comedy and bizarre intensity of the face-off created one of the most talked-about television moments of the season. By leaning entirely into the surreal nature of the original documentary, Druski solidified his hosting debut as a major comedic success that pushed the boundaries of traditional late-night television.
